DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph DILG OPINION No. 16 s. 2022 MAR 10, 2022 DIR. JOSEPHINE CABRIDO-LEYSA Regional Director — DILG Region XII Prime Regional Government Center. Carpenter Hill, Koronadal City Dear Director Cabrido-Leysa: This has reference to your letter dated 06 January 2022 seeking legal opinion from this Department on whether or not the RPOC Head Secretariat may issue Peace and Order Program Certification to the Province of Cotabato based on their re-enacted budget for FY 2022, in relation to Section 323 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) and the interim NPOC Advisory No. 2016-02 dated November 25, 2016. Per your letter, for failure of the Sanggunian Panlalawigan to pass the budget ordinance for the current year, the Local Government Unit of Cotabato is now on a reenacted budget following Section 323 of the LGC, viz: "Section 323. Failure to Enact the Annual Appropriations. - In case the sanggunian concemed fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may be taken up during such sessions. If the sanggunian still fails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and effect until the ordinance authonzing the proposed appropriations is passed by the sanggunian concemed. However, only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith." In the implementation of such reenacted ordinance, the local treasurer concerned shall exclude from the estimates of income for the preceding fiscal year those realized from nonrecurring sources, like national aids, proceeds from loans, sale of assets, prior year adjustments, and other analogous sources of income. No ordinance authorizing supplemental appropriations shall be passed in place of the annual appropriations. X x x x" (Emphasis and underlining supplied) "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

The above-mentioned provision specifically provides that the reenacted budget shall remain in force and effect until the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations is passed by the sanggunian concerned. Hence, by necessary implication, the budget appropriated for the preceding year shall remain in force and effect Per Item 4.10 of DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019-43, Peace and Order Programs (POP) includes projects, programs and activities (PPAs) that directly address criminality, armed conflict, and human rights violations and bring about the achievement of justice, peace and order. For its funding requirements, Item 7.1.3(0 states: "This Chapter applies the Annual Investment Program (AIP) as a required template for writing the funding proposal for submission to the Sanggunian for the indicative annual expenditure of the local govemment. It includes the detailed annual allocation for PPPSAs and in the regular operaåonal budget items broken down into Personnel Services (PS), Maintenance and Other Operaång Expenses (MOOE), and Capital Ouåay (CO). An Annual Investment Program or Plan and a narrative of Regulatory Measures are needed to complete this chapter. (Emphasis supplied) Annual Investment Program pursuant to DILG-NEDA-DBM-DOF Joint Memorandum Circular No. 1, Series of 20161 refers to the annual slice of the Local Development Investment Program (LDIP), which constitutes the total resource requirements for all Programs, Projects and Activities (PPAs) consisting of the annual capital expenditure and regular operating requirements of the LGU. It is emphasized herein that only the following are deemed reenacted: (1) annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions; (2) statutory and contractual obligations; and (3) essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year. There is a difference between MOOE and essential operating expenses, MOOE is defined under the Glossary of Terms, Operating Manual for Local Govemment Units 2016 Edition as an allocation to support the operations of local government units including those for supplies and materials, transportation and travel, utilities and other maintenance activities. On the other hand, essential operating expenses pursuant to Second Paragraph, Item 1.5, Page 67 of the Budget Operations Manual for Local Govemment Units 2016 Edition, refers to specific objects of expenditure under maintenance and other operating expense, which are necessary for the operation of a particular local govemment unit to carry out its mandate in providing efficient and effective basic services2. The Department in its Legal Opinion No. 42, s.2018 has opined that only essential (of the utmost importance; indispensable; extremely necessary) and not all operating expenses should be included in the MOOE. In view thereof, the Department qualifies its response to the query. Ifthe annual budget of the preceding year certifies that the Peace and Order Program is an essential operating expense to be charged under MOOE, then the POP certificate may be issued under a reenacted budget. If such was not stated in the annual budget of the previous 1 Dated November 18, 2016 2 DILG Legal Opinion No. 71,5.2019 Page 2 of 3

year, no POP Certificate may be issued. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion that will be rendered by more competent authority and courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN Underse tary for Local Government OUSLG/MLl/LLLS-LRALLD/lasm/rrao Page 3 of 3
